I have encountered quite a few posts recently related to Israel in which it seems that OP / commenter are confusing the following three terms: Jews (the Jewish people), the Jewish religion (Judaism) and Zionism - causing confusion and creating disinformation.

I thought I would make this post which can be used as reference in such cases where one of these terms is confused with another or is simply referenced inaccurately.

....

1. The Jews (the Jewish people)

The Jews are an ethnic group or ethnicity. They are an ethnoreligious and ethno-cultural group descended from the Israelites of the Ancient Near East and originating from the historical kingdoms of Israel and Judah.

A Jew who lives in Israel is an Israeli-Jew in the same way that an Irish living in the US is... an Irish-American. One does not become a Jew in the same way one does become Irish - it is a heritage - if one or both of your parents are Irish then you are Irish / part Irish as well. In the same way, if one or both your parents were Jews then you are a Jew / part Jew. (*note: Jewish orthodox Jews only consider a person who's mother is Jewish to be a Jew)

A Jew can be of any religion (Christian Jew, Muslim Jew, Jewish Jew etc.) in the same way an Irish person can be of any religion (Protestant / Catholic Christian Irish, Muslim Irish, Jewish Irish etc.).

....

2. The Jewish religion (Judaism)

Judaism is an ancient monotheistic religion, with the Torah as its foundational text (part of the larger text known as the Tanakh or Hebrew Bible). Judaism is considered by religious Jews to be the expression of the covenantal relationship that God established with the Children of Israel. Similarly to Christianity, Islam and other religions, there are many, many sects in Judaism (Orthodox Judaism, Reform Judaism, Conservative Judaism, Hasidic Judaism etc.). This would be the equivalent of sects such as Protestant, Catholic, Evangelical etc. Christianity.

The Jewish religion, while not a missionary religion like Christianity for example, is open for anyone to join. One does not have to be a Jew in order to become Jewish, nevertheless, the process of becoming Jewish is very different for someone who is not a Jew and is called "Giyur".

The Israeli government / state / regime was originally founded as a home for the Jewish people with a completely secular outlook, however over the years and with the gain in power of various religious / nationalist-religious groups, the secular character of state is being replaced by various Jewish (religious) interests which are then forced upon the Israeli population (both Jews and non Jews).

....

3. Zionism

Zionism is a nationalist and political movement that supports the re-establishment of a Jewish homeland in the territory defined as the historic Land of Israel (historical kingdoms of Israel and Judah / now: Israel / Palestine). Just like with any national / political movement, there are various sub sects / ideologies of Zionism (Labor Zionism, Liberal Zionism, Nationalist Zionism, Religious Zionism etc.)

The Israeli government / state / regime has always embraced and implemented a Zionist ideology to varying extents since its establishment, depending on the political parties in power.

Contrary to the common misconceptions I have encountered here on Voat - one does not need to be a Jew or Jewish (religious) in order to be a Zionist.
